# Independent audit of the two new projective continuations

Source: `candidate c56743c8d6824a18`, Sections6--8.

Result: PASS. This extends my earlier Sections1--5 audit; no efficiency
claim for arbitrary bodies is inferred.

1. The normal variable is a unit vector. Consequently the two centers in
(20) have signed support distances exactly s=H-Delta and midpoint y.
Where the cutoff is nonzero, s>=r/2. The convex field coefficients are
nonnegative and the interior-reference terms are positive. Compactness
makes the resulting fields continuous and bounded on actual bodies.

2. In the full-field band, equal-weight Jensen yields precisely the
middle field with coefficient s. Replacing s by H incurs Delta*e*f,
which the original Delta gap pays whenever e*f<=1. Outside that band,
including the cutoff transition, Delta>delta and nestedness preserves
the original support gap. The separate uniform bound (23) pays the
entire desired middle erosion. Thus all normal inequalities hold
simultaneously, without a hull repair or y in the midpoint body.

3. The tangent extension of t^(-d) is decreasing everywhere. The actual
a-minimizing partner therefore gives the direction of (25) exactly as
printed. Each one-sided field alone supplies twice the middle field;
the two complementary coefficients sum to one. Averaging the actual
input support inequalities proves exact compatibility. A zero
coefficient leaves the corresponding body fixed.

4. The new fields meet all the continuum-normal first-variation
hypotheses already audited in Section3. Formula(26) is linear in the
mixing coefficient because the first boundary costs are linear in the
field. The full/empty/supporting statuses retain their separate
interpretations; no closed boundary atom is silently charged.

5. The actual rational calibration uses the separately certified
all-normal triangle depth formula. The normal-center path has loss12,
cost27 and payment12/601. The one-input path has cost261/10 and
payment252/601. Its original fixed caps differ from the optimized caps
by4e^2, so the same derivative is valid without claiming exact
post-deformation criticality of the old caps. The strict endpoint gap
continues to give global, rather than source-only, descent.

The companion source
`candidate 358e239a9d0e9d92`
shows why these new paths are outside the whole old common-perspective
field class: every field in that class has nonpositive payment on this
same actual triple, by a facetwise reversed-Chebyshev inequality.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
